refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: The vera system process runs as PID 1 and is responsible for starting and stopping major system processes, including system startup and shutdown. vera also listens on an internal socket for commands that adjust the system running state. The vlad command connects to that internal socket and passes along the commands (that vlad doesn't handle by itself).

Installing vera does not automatically replace the default init supervisor. This manual page describes the process for converting an existing system from init to vera, and restoring a converted system back to init. This manual page also describes some common and less common management commands.

See
vera.runlevels 8
for a description of how vera manages runlevels, starts, and stops individual units or processes.

See
vera.units 8
for more information on adding custom units and processes to vera, and
vera.sessions 8
for more information on managing session units.

See
vera.logs 8
for more information on obtaining basic statistics on processes started by vera.

See
vera.extras 8
for more information on additional features that vera adds to a base Slackware system.

refsect1.title: MANAGING vera
refsect1.para: vlad vera-up tries to connect to vera's public socket. A successful connection indicates that vera is installed and running. This is indicated by a 0 exit code. A connection failure causes it to terminate with a non-0 exit code (no error message is shown).

Installing vera (from a package or by make install) does not touch or replace the default system init daemon. Additional commands must be executed, and a coordinated reboot is required in order to roll the dice, and start vera.
The hook and hookonce commands begin the process of converting from init to vera. They make the following changes:

listitem.para: The original /sbin/init gets moved to /sbin/init.init.

The original /etc/rc.d/rc.sysvinit, /etc/rc.d/rc.local and /etc/rc.d/rc.local_shutdown, scripts get moved to /etc/rc.d/rc.sysvinit.init, /etc/rc.d/rc.local.init and /etc/rc.d/rc.local_shutdown.init, if they exist. The original /usr/sbin/logrotate binary gets moved to /usr/sbin/logrotate.init.
The moved scripts and binaries get replaced with links to vera's replacements.
@CONFIGDIR@/hook gets created.

refsect1.para: The installed rc script replacements check if vera-up is running; if so, they do nothing because the inittab command installs units that run these scripts and commands. Otherwise, if vera-up is not running and init is still running (prior to or after a reboot), the replacements execute the replaced program or script, with no change in behavior.

The replacement /usr/sbin/logrotate script checks if vera-up is running; if so, the original /usr/sbin/logrotate.init runs with a different configuration, /etc/logrotate.conf.vera. Otherwise, if vera-up is not running and init is still running (prior to or after a reboot), /usr/sbin/logrotate.init runs with the default /etc/logrotate.conf configuration.

An installed container, system/update-logrotate runs a script when the system boots. This script reads /etc/logrotate.conf and /etc/logrotate.d, and creates /etc/logrotate.conf.vera and /etc/logrotate.d.vera. Every reference in logrotate's scripts that runs /etc/rc.d/name restart or /etc/rc.d/name reload gets replaced with the equivalent vlad command.
The replacement /sbin/init, called vera-init, checks that @CONFIGDIR@/hook exists on the next reboot, and starts vera instead of the replaced init.

hookonce results in the removal of @CONFIGDIR@/hook on the next reboot as early as possible. Its absence on a subsequent reboot results in the original init (now /sbin/init.init) starting normally as PID 1.

The unhook command manually removes @CONFIGDIR@/hook. If the system was booted with vera, no further action is taken. A reboot is required to start the system with the original init; then the unhook command must be executed a second time. This completes the process of reverting back to init.
When unhook determines that vera-up is not running, unhook restores the scripts and binaries that hook originally moved.

note.para: Do not run make uninstall to completely uninstall vera unless it's fully unhooked.
Do not update sysvinit and logrotate unless vera is fully unhooked.

refsect1.para: The inittab command rereads /etc/inittab, /etc/rc.d/rc.M, and /etc/rc.d/rc?.d directories, translates them to unit specification files in @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@. A brief overview of the translation process for entries in the /etc/inittab file:

listitem.para: All keywordwait entries get created as forking start types; respawn as respawn; and all others as oneshot.
powerstate, ctrlaltdel, and boot are added to the corresponding target.
boot and bootwait entries get added as dependencies of system/boot, which is a dependency of all runlevels; in this manner, these entries get executed before all runlevels' entries.
Each entry's one-character runlevels get converted to the corresponding vera runlevel targets, and the entry becomes a dependency of the runlevel target.
Entries that match the names of selected /etc/rc.d/rc.X scripts get singled out for special processing.
Before and After get specified for each converted inittab entry, that starts them (and stops them in reverse order) in order of appearance in /etc/inittab.
The @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@/system/inittab directory gets created or updated with units that run each /etc/inittab entry.

refsect1.para: The /etc/rc.d/rc.M script's contents are searched for every instance of -x /etc/rc.d/rc.script followed by /etc/rc.d/rc.script start. This creates a corresponding @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@/system/rc.M/rc.script unit that runs /etc/rc.d/rc.script start and /etc/rc.d/rc.script stop. The entry for /etc/rc.d/rc.M executes it via a wrapper that converts it, on the fly, to start each corresponding unit, instead of running each script directly.
Finally, entries in /etc/rc.d/rc?.d get translated to unit files as follows:

listitem.para: All files with names that don't start with S and K get ignored. Files containing whitespace, a ~, or a # get ignored; otherwise:
Every file's (device and) inode gets looked up. All S files named the same, but in different /etc/rc.d/rc?.d directories must have the same (device and) inode.
This verifies that the same S file in every /etc/rc.d/rc?.d directory is the same script.

The @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@/system/rc directory gets created or updated with units that run each script from the /etc/rc.d/rc?.d, and the converted units are dependencies of the corresponding vera runlevel target.
Each unit's starting command runs the S script with the start parameter.

The existence of a K file with the same (device and) inode results in the unit's stopping command getting set, which runs the script with the stop parameter. Otherwise there is no explicit stopping command.
If the S or K scripts are symbolic links the commands are updated to reflect the symlink target name, as syntactic sugar.

refsect1.para: The rehook command checks that at least one of the files that the hook command saves as the original file exists. This indicates that vera is currently hooked. If not, rehook does nothing. Otherwise, the list of files that get saved is checked, and if the original copy of that file does not exist it is made from the current file, and vera's file is hooked into place. This would occur when updating vera to a newer version that hooks an additional file.

The inittab and rehook commands run automatically when vera gets updated. The vera package installs binaries named vlad-inst, vera-inst, and an installation script checks whether vlad and vera exist, and hard-links them if not. If they exist the existing binaries are left untouched. They are the current active binaries. The vera package also installs a vera-init binary which gets linked as /sbin/init.

refsect1.title: Internal commands
refsect1.para: These commands are for internal use only, and are only documented here for completeness.

sysdown directs vera on PID 1 to set the RUNLEVEL environment variable and execute a specified script, replacing PID 1. This is used as a final action for executing a shutdown or a reboot (the rc.0 and rc.6 scripts).

The vera-init executable gets linked as /sbin/init and it performs a delicate juggling act of switching between vera and the legacy init command, which gets renamed as /sbin/init.init by the hook command.

When it's not started as PID 1 vera-init determines whether the system was booted by vera or init by connecting to vera's internal communication socket. A connection failure indicates that vera is hooked as /sbin/init but the system has not been rebooted yet, so vera-init executes /sbin/init.init and forwards all parameters to it. A successful connection indicates that vera is running. vera-init executes the vlad command and forwards its arguments to it.
When started as PID 1 vera-init determines whether the system should be booted by the legacy init or vera.

listitem.para: Absence of /sbin/init.init indicates that vera is installed and the legacy init is removed. vera is the only option.
@CONFIGDIR@/hook is checked, this file is updated by hook, hookonce and unhook commands.

If @CONFIGDIR@/hook exists but its timestamp is identical to /proc/1's timestamp then this is treated as if it does not exist. hook/hookonce intentionally sets the hook file's timestamp like this. init executes itself before a reboot, and this is used to detect this edge case. Even though this is PID 1, the system has not been started by vera.
The absence of @CONFIGDIR@/hook results in executing /sbin/init.init, the legacy init.
A hookonce removes @CONFIGDIR@/hook, for the next boot.

At this point a final determination is made that the system is getting booted by vera. Before this happens vera-init reads /etc/inittab and directly runs all sysinit commands, then executes vera to start the rest of the system.

refsect1.para: Before executing the sysdown script, a check is made whether vera-init is different from the current /sbin/init. The same check is made with vlad-inst and vera-inst; they are checked to see if they differ from vlad and vera respectively. If they are different it must mean that an updated vera package was installed, so the new binaries replace the active binaries. vera does not implement a reexec-based approach to activating a new version in a live system. Instead, the newer version is activated when the system shuts down.

refsect1.title: BUGS
refsect1.para: The vera and vlad commands are not named after any well-known public figures.
vera does not implement /var/run/runlevel.
vera does not implement /dev/initctl.

Updating sysvinit after hooking into and starting vera results in a mostly bricked system that will not shut down properly, but will probably reboot into the original init if all filesystems are fully synced before forcing the reboot. Do not update sysvinit before fully unhooking vera (twice) and rebooting back into init (see for more information).
system/rc.M units always claim they're manually started, even though they get started automatically. This is an artifact of how vera's inittab command works.
